producer_report.summary: Root cause: refusal and matching rules (parts parser, stems, stop lists, reading checks) were specified by reasoning and hand-checked on a few cases, and nothing ran them against real request and reading shapes before they were planned or landed. The gaps (N. and N) parts, stop-list/stem order, a job cited but not relied on, brand words read as symbols) therefore showed up only in critic rounds. The fix is at the shared gate and the planning rule, not in one job's check. (1) reading.rs gains `refusing_check`, which runs the six existing checks in the same order from one `step!` line each and returns the first refusing check's name (via `stringify!`) with its error. `check_reading_acceptance` is now a thin wrapper, so outcomes and error text are unchanged and no refusal rule is tightened. (2) New `crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs` stores 19 labeled shapes (source job, rebuilt from the job brief, form tags, pinned bullet count, expected outcome). They cover Steward dash bullets, star bullets, `1.` parts, the `1)` and `(a)` parts the parser does not read today (pinned as a known gap), a root-cause request citing two rejected jobs, a follow-up line, retry complaints that name and omit the job, producer-report evidence, code survey, governance, crate-relative path, absent path, and GitHub/env-var tokens. (3) Mechanism tests: every `step!(check_*(` in `refusing_check` must have a corpus case where that check refuses; a doctored copy of the real source with one invented step is reported; `check_reading_acceptance` may not call a check directly; a form-coverage test fixes the list of input forms. (4) planner.md gets one short clause (`Refusal or matching rule: map each input form to a refusal_corpus case.`), paid for by trimming existing words so it stays 1439 bytes and the composed planner size stays 806. The planner brief's Report section carries the full rule (list input forms, read the corpus file and map each to a case id or list the case a step adds, make `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` the producer and verifier demonstration, and do not cite results the planner could not run). (5) A briefs test pins both texts. CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md (D148) name the root cause, the relation to the verify-time replay (unchanged), the residual parser/stem/stop-list limit, and the follow-ups.

open_issues: The fixture request texts are rebuilt from the job briefs and labeled 'rebuilt from the job brief' because records/ is absent from the snapshot; stored verbatim text can replace them later.
The `1)` and `(a)` cases pin today's parser result (0 bullets), a known gap; the parts-coverage follow-up must change those counts on purpose.

The mechanism sees `check_*` steps only. A new helper inside an existing check, or a change to is_bullet, request_text_acceptance, stems or stop lists, is narrowed by the pinned bullet counts and the form-coverage test, and otherwise rests on the planner rule, which is prose only.

'Run the rule against the corpus and cite the results' is implemented as map-to-case-ids plus a named producer/verifier demonstration, because the planner cannot run commands. This follows the plan's open question; the brief wording differs.
mistakes: First draft of refusal_corpus.rs used `Vec::new()` then `out.push(...)` and a stray `{marker}` format argument; both were caught by the compiler and clippy and fixed.

A messy intermediate edit while splitting the case builders into three functions left a placeholder and mismatched delimiters in the test file; fixed before any test run. The final file compiles and passes.
planner.md first came out at 1441 bytes (807 tokens composed), which failed the budgets test; trimmed two bytes.
learnings: estimate_tokens is ceil(bytes/3); planner.md is capped under 500 tokens (<=1497 bytes) and the composed planner size is pinned in docs/system-facts.md (806). Two extra bytes tipped it to 807 and failed the budgets test, so the final planner.md is exactly its old size, 1439 bytes.
The planner has Read/Grep/Glob only, so a rule that tells it to 'run' a corpus must be worded as map-and-name for the producer and verifier.
clippy's vec_init_then_push fires on `Vec::new()` followed straight by `push`, including in test fixtures; build the first element in a `vec![]`.

Integration tests in athena-core can use the crate's normal dependencies (jiff, anyhow, athena_data, athena_context) and include_str!("../src/reading.rs") for source-scanning, like external_calls_guard.rs.
docs/decisions.md ended at D147 and there is no registry (decision-links.toml, ontology) that has to list a new D number.
